newsitem.title: INDIA: India's new privatisation goal said more credible.
newsitem.headline: India's new privatisation goal said more credible.

text.p: India expects a more buoyant stock market to help it meet a target of selling 48 billion rupees' ($1.3) worth of shares in state firms in 1997/98 (April-March), a senior Finance Ministry official said on Saturday.

Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia told a news conference that the government failed to meet its 1996/97 goal of taking in 50 billion rupees in partial privatisation proceeds due to depressed capital markets and procedural delays.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday while presenting the 1997/98 budget that the government aims to sell 48 billion rupees' worth of shares in state firms in the next fiscal year.
Budget documents showed that the government has set a new target for 1996/97 of five billion rupees.

The government had earlier announced plans to sell a seven percent stake in telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in oil refiner Indian Oil Corp (IOC) in the first round of divestment in 1996/97.
But the government has not yet fixed a date for kicking off the first round.

"Partly because we had adopted a new procedure which took some time to generate recommendations, and partly because of market conditions, it was not possible to reach this year's target," Ahluwalia said.
He was referring to the establishment last year of the Disinvestment Commission.
India, which started partial privatisation under an economic reform programme launched in 1991, set up the commission last year to advise a strategy for disinvestment of shares in 40 state firms.
Ahluwalia said investors were more upbeat about the Indian economy.
"We also feel that the present perception both of domestic buyers and buyers of the Indian economy is much stronger than it might have been several months ago," he said.
"I would say the target of 48 billion rupees which has been set for 97/98 is qualitatively a far more credible target than 50 billion turned out to be for 96/97," he said.

Chidambaram told parliament the government planned to sell its stakes in three state-controlled firms -- Gas Authority of India Ltd, Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd and the Indian Tourism Development Corp -- as suggested by the Disinvestment Commission. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
